dedupe_keys.name: the nutritious supply chain optimising wfp humanitarian food assistance in iraq yemen and the 2016 el nino drought

description: This case study describes the optimisation model the World Food Programme developed to plan humanitarian food assistance, reaching about 90 million people in 80 countries a year. The authors, from WFP's supply chain optimisation team and Tilburg University, published it in the INFORMS Journal on Optimization. A mixed integer linear programme simultaneously chooses the food basket, the sourcing plan, the delivery plan and the transfer modality, cash or in kind, for each month of a long-term recovery operation, linking supply chain decisions to nutritional objectives. Coverage is WFP operations, with examples from Iraq, Yemen and southern Africa. The article is free to read on the publisher's site as open access, though no reuse licence is stated in the metadata. Caveats: the model and operational data are internal to WFP, results are reported for selected operations, and costs and nutrient values depend on WFP's planning data. The authors show three uses: cutting operational costs in Iraq by 12 percent without reducing nutritional value, managing the scale-up of the Yemen operation from three to six million beneficiaries, and identifying sourcing strategies during the 2016 El Niño drought. Simulation uses: an example of optimisation for food supply chains in emergency response, reusable for disruption and drought scenarios. Related records: WFP HungerMap LIVE (platform-wfp-hungermap-live) supplies related operational information.
